chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who spends the night in a house alone, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, and if he is compelled to do so, then there is no problem, but he should increase the remembrance of Allah in his sleep as much as he can.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and recommendation for a man who sleeps alone in a house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the juristic principle of 'karahat' (dislike) rather than prohibition for sleeping alone, accommodating human necessity while encouraging spiritual vigilance. The recommendation to engage in dhikr during sleep reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining a state of divine awareness even in states of unconsciousness, thereby transforming a potentially fearful solitude into an act of worship. This practice aligns with the broader tradition of viewing sleep as a 'minor death' requiring spiritual preparation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sleeps alone in a house, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislke that, and if he is desperate to that, so there is no problem, but he should frequent in the mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during his sleep for as long as he can’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sleeps in a house alone. He (the Imam) said, ‘I dislike it but if it is an emergency, then it is not harmful, however, he must speak of Allah a great deal and as much as he can, when he goes to sleep.’”
